title: Fractions Worksheets: Halves, Thirds, and Fourths
intro: Teach equal area as the essential feature of fractional parts.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Have the student divide a rectangle into equal-area parts and shade one. Compare different valid partitions.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Three equal parts need two dividing lines.

To make three equal strips, mark about one third and two thirds of the rectangle's width. Draw a straight line at each mark, then shade one strip. Count the spaces, not the lines.

Ask your student

How could we check that the parts have equal area?

If your student needs help

If the student makes unequal parts, use folding or a grid to compare their sizes.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each sheet asks for halves, thirds, and fourths once, using the same original rectangle shape. The answer key gives checking guidance rather than a single completed drawing, because more than one partition can be correct. New numbers does not change these three fixed tasks.
